nuggets.text: Alex Golesh was born in Moscow and moved to the United States at age seven as the Soviet Union was breaking up.
Byrum Brown followed Alex Golesh from South Florida to Auburn, reuniting quarterback and coach on the Plains.
Byrum Brown passed for 3,000 yards and ran for 1,000 at USF in 2025, the 12th FBS player to do both in one season.
Saturday is the Tigers' home opener and Alex Golesh's first game on the Jordan-Hare Stadium sideline.
The Tigers beat Baylor 17-16 in the opener, and the defense forced takeaways on the game's first two plays.
Jordan-Hare drew 88,043 for Argentina vs. Iceland in June, the biggest soccer crowd in Alabama history.
Jordan-Hare became the first stadium in the country named for an active coach when Shug Jordan's name was added in 1973.
The Tigers' War Eagle cry lives on with a live golden eagle that flies over the stadium before home games.
Tigers fans celebrate wins by rolling the trees at Toomer's Corner in toilet paper, a tradition dating to 1972.
The Tigers have three Heisman Trophy winners: Pat Sullivan in 1971, Bo Jackson in 1985 and Cam Newton in 2010.
